notes.1a: This question was answered well by the majority of candidates. The most common error was to match the function of the anther to the function of the stigma.
notes.1b: This structure of pollen grains was well known and good responses were seen. Errors include responses that were not comparative but instead stated features of wind-pollinated and insect- pollinated pollen.
notes.1c: Again responses were generally very good. The most common errors were the type of reproduction and the substances that were absorbed by roots.
notes.2a: Some candidates knew the features of arthropods with most giving the correct response the group with four pairs of legs. The other two characteristics were less well known.
notes.2b: The majority of candidates gave correct responses. The commonest error was just to repeat the characteristics stated in Question 2(a) .
notes.2cii: Most candidates gave the correct response. Occasionally the statement was the wrong way round i.e. as the rate of movement increases so temperature increases implying the rate of movement is causing an increase in temperature. Less well-executed response only quoted figures with no reference to the trend.
notes.2ciii: This proved to be a challenging question. A common incorrect response was (5÷9.5) ⋅ 100 = 52.6%.
notes.3a: The majority of candidates gave correct responses to this question. The most common errors were for the last part ‘where the most water is absorbed’.
notes.3bi: Some candidates gave the correct response. Many gave the type of disease rather than the type of pathogen.
notes.3bii: A few knew the definition of the term. Common incorrect responses described the consequences of diarrhoea rather than what it was.
notes.3biii: Some candidates gave a correct response.
notes.3c: Generally well answered. The most common correct responses were skin and hairs in nose. Some incorrectly gave medical sources of protection such as vaccinations and antibiotics which did not answer the question.
notes.4a: Very well answered. The commonest incorrect response was to identify the vacuole as the nucleus.
notes.4bi: As so many had got the first part of the question correct, candidates seem to be able to recognise cell structure, but fewer were able to describe the changes that had taken place in the cell. Many wrote about the cell contents going into the vacuole and others explained why this happened (answering part (ii) in part (i) ). The most common responses were the vacuole and cytoplasm shrinking or reducing in size.
notes.4bii: Generally not as well answered as the previous part. The best responses gave a good explanation using the term osmosis. Some answered part (i) in part (ii) . Some incorrectly wrote about the sugar solution moving rather than the water, others wrote about the water going in the wrong direction.
notes.4biii: Most were able to understand that by placing the cell in water or a less concentrated solution, the cell could be returned to its original appearance.
notes.4ci: Very well answered with the majority giving the correct response and very few stating phloem.
notes.5a: Many candidates knew that herbivores feed on plants or producers, fewer referred to energy.
notes.5b: Increased food and decreased predation were the most common correct responses.
notes.5c: Many good responses were seen. Some only described different forms of pollution and made no reference to overfishing, the effects on food chains or the extinction of species. Some gave reasons why the human population was increasing and many referred to deforestation which did not answer the question.
notes.6a: The majority of candidates gave the correct responses. Common incorrect responses included sperm duct, oviduct and ovules.
notes.6bi: Again well answered by the majority of candidates. The commonest incorrect responses were embryo or fetus instead of zygote and ovule instead of ovum.
notes.6bii: Only a few candidates gave the correct responses. Some gave XX or XY for the gametes and some did not realise that the embryo was female and gave XY for the zygote. A few gave a numerical value.
notes.6biii: Most candidates identified fertilisation but fewer identified mitosis.
notes.6biv: Most correctly gave uterus. A few stated placenta.
notes.6c: Most candidates knew examples of barrier and chemical methods of contraception but fewer were able to give examples of surgical and natural methods of contraception.
notes.7a: Well answered by the majority of candidates.
